# **ESM 232 Assignment 2**

The goal for this assignment is to implement a simple model of almond yield anomaly response to climate.

# **Conceptual Model**

We used the Lobell et al. 2006 paper as the source for the transfer function that we use in the conceptual model, specifically looking at the equations in table 2. The conceptual model (embed as picture) shows how we applied the function to the test climate data (clim.txt).

![](images/Almond%20Yield%20Diagram.jpg)

# Libraries

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
```

# Load data

```{r}
clim <- read.table(here("data", "clim.txt"), header = TRUE, sep = " ")
```

# Filter data

Filter the climate dataset to only include January (1) and February (2). These are the months used in the almond yield model.

```{r}
filtered_clim <- clim |>
  filter(month %in% c(1, 2)) |>
  select(-wy, -tmax_c)
```

# Average February minimum temperature

```{r}
feb_avg <- filtered_clim %>%
  filter(month == 2) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(feb_avg_min_temp = mean(tmin_c, na.rm = TRUE))
```

# Total January precipitation

```{r}
jan_sum <- filtered_clim %>%
  filter(month == 1) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(jan_total_precip = sum(precip, na.rm = TRUE))
```

When using the mean minimum temperature, the output stats should be:

max: 1919.98, min: -0.35, mean: 181.44
